title: uuencoding::decode_limited splits all input into lines upfront, defeating the max_bytes limit for large inputs
description:
## Problem

In `uuencoding/src/decode.rs`, `decode_limited(input, max_bytes)` begins by:

```rust
let lines: Vec<&[u8]> = input.split(|&b| b == b'\n').collect();
```

This splits the ENTIRE input into a `Vec` of line slices before any decoding occurs, regardless of the `max_bytes` limit. For a 100 MiB UU-encoded body with `max_bytes = 1024`, the function allocates and iterates over roughly 2 million line entries before stopping at the limit.

## Documented in the docstring but underemphasised

The function docstring notes: 'Memory used by this function is O(max_bytes) for output but O(input) for the internal line split'. This is documented, but only in a buried note that callers frequently miss.

## What goes wrong

A JMAP server or mail client calling `decode_body_value(raw, part, Some(4096))` on a large attachment (e.g. a 50 MiB UU-encoded file in a text/plain body) will allocate and scan the full 50 MiB of line pointers even though the request is for only 4 KiB of decoded output. The `max_bytes` parameter does not bound memory consumption or CPU time — it only limits the OUTPUT size.

`mime-tree::decode_body_value` calls `decode_limited` for `TransferEncoding::UUencode` parts, so this path is reachable by any caller of `decode_body_value` with a `max_bytes` limit.

## Files

- `uuencoding/src/decode.rs` — `decode_limited` function
- `mime-tree/src/decode.rs` — calls `decode_limited` for UUencode transfer encoding

## What goes wrong if left as-is

Callers who set `max_bytes` to bound resource consumption during MIME preview generation will be surprised to find that UUencode parts consume O(input) resources anyway. This is a correctness violation of the implied contract of `max_bytes`.
close_reason: Replaced upfront Vec line split with LazyLines iterator. decode_limited now scans O(bytes consumed) not O(total input).
